correctness.rationale: The frozen estimate is valid: its truncation step must use r^{M+1}/(1−r) as a common upper bound for operator and symbol errors, not assert a pointwise symbol bound by the actual operator norm. The repaired proof instead gives a sharper quantitative claim by an exact form reduction. Unitary weight transfer gives A=D(I−rS)^{-1} with closed inverse B=(I−rS)J on dom J; B*B=(AA*)^{-1}. The form on the circle with p(θ)=1+r²−2r cos θ has entries jk p̂(j−k). Modes of opposite sign cannot couple via this bandwidth, and mode zero decouples. The positive-mode block is B*B; reflection gives the other copy, so the unweighted singular index matches precisely the nth pair of positive periodic eigenvalues. The Liouville variable and multiplier z=p^{1/4} give the periodic potential V=z″/z, whose mean is ∫(z′/z)²/L=μ_r>0. Min–max locates the eigenvalue pair within bounded distance of (n/κ)²; on its complement the free resolvent is O_q(n^{-1}). Within the pair the diagonal potential is μ_r and the other entries are Fourier coefficients O_q(n^{-1}). Thus the squared inverse singular value is (n/κ)²+μ_r+O_q(n^{-1}); inverse square roots prove the correction, and inversion gives a bounded counting remainder. This uses the infinite closed forms, not a finite-section inference.

value.rationale: The first nonvanishing correction for the singular rather than ordinary eigenvalues resolves the order and sign of the deviation from the already known leading law. The gain is structural, not just a smaller bound: the inverse form converts an infinite nonnormal averaging problem to half the positive spectrum of an explicit periodic differential operator and yields a constant-error count. The positive coefficient rules out a little-o of n^{-3} leading remainder at every fixed nonzero weight.
